name: Home Assistant Control Center
tagline: Secure Home Assistant control and identity verification for Anna
description:
Home Assistant Control Center connects Anna to the Home Assistant server you already use. Ask Anna in chat for a room’s temperature, check whether a light is on, or control a device you’ve allowed Anna to use. Use Control Center to test the connection, manage permissions, and review actions that need your approval.

Once connected, Anna can read sensors by default. Other device access starts disabled. For each category, such as lights, switches, thermostats, or locks, choose Disabled, Enabled, or Verify. With Verify, Anna holds the action until you review the exact request and approve it in Control Center with a PIN or authenticator code.

The setup guide walks you through choosing an Anna Agent, creating a Home Assistant access token, and testing the connection. You’ll need your own running Home Assistant server. An Anna Cloud Agent needs a publicly reachable HTTPS address. A Linux x86-64 Local Agent can connect to a Home Assistant server it can reach on your home network.

Enter your server address and access token in Anna’s secure Connector settings. When you change permissions, Control Center guides you through applying them and checking which settings are active.
